sentences.text:
Heard Sri Amit Saxena, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Pankaj Dubey, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri M.C. Chaturvedi, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Suresh C. Dwivedi,
learned counsel for respondent No.2 as well as learned Standing Counsel for the State.
2. By means of the present petition, the petitioner has challenged the notifications dated 16.10.2004 and 28.10.2005 issued u/s 4(1) and 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, respectively.

3. From perusal of the record, it appears that the validity of impugned notifications came to be considered before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 11501 of 2016 (M/s Sahara India Commercial Corporation Ltd. and others vs. State of U.P. and others) with other connected civil appeals.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No. 11501 of 2016 (M/s Sahara India Commercial Corporation Ltd. and others vs. State of U.P. and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Above bunch of cases were disposed of by Hon'ble Supreme Court by judgement dated 30.11.2016 and Hon'ble Court was pleased to hold that the impugned notification was issued without holding enquiry/hearing of objection u/s 5A of the Land Acquisition Act, therefore, the same would not be justified and acquisition proceeding as a whole would be open for interference,

but Hon'ble Supreme Court also observed that despite interference in the acquisition proceedings by this Court, the acquiring authority will not be under obligation to return any part of the land to any of the land owners.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court further directed in the above judgement that all the petitioners will be entitled to compensation as per the new Act (Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013) by treating the date of this order as date for fresh notification for acquisition of aforesaid land.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner prayed that this writ petition may be disposed of in terms of the above order of Hon'ble Supreme Court.

4. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 objected to the aforesaid prayer of the petitioner on the ground that present petition suffers from laches and during the pendency of present writ petition,
the award for acquired land of the petitioner was already delivered in the year 2013.

sentences.text: Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of record, this Court finds that the present writ petition was filed in 2009 and an order of status quo was also passed on 10.9.2009.

Subsequently, this writ petition was dismissed for want of prosecution on 21.1.2010 and the same was restored on 12.2.2014 on the basis of recall/restoration application filed in the year 2010 itself.

Thereafter, this writ petition was again dismissed for want of prosecution on 23.4.2015 but the same was restored by this Court by order dated 4.8.2016 and present writ petition is pending for disposal since then.

During pendency of this writ petition, the award regarding land of the petitioner was passed in the year 2013 though litigation regarding aforesaid notification was pending before Hon'ble Supreme Court since 2010 and same was disposed of by judgement dated 30.11.2016, therefore, the present petition cannot be dismissed on the ground of laches and petitioner cannot be deprived of benefit of order dated 30.11.2016 of Hon'ble Supreme Court.
6.

In view of the above, the present writ petition is disposed of with direction that the petitioner will also be entitled to benefit granted to other land holders by judgement dated 30.11.2016 of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 11501 of 2016.

7. As the award regarding land of the petitioner has been delivered during pendency of the present petition in 2013, therefore, the same deserves to be quashed and new award regarding acquired land of the petitioner should be calculated as per judgement dated 30.11.2016 of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
